headline_marked: Rain washout: [[Bangladesh reach Asian Games semi-finals]] without playing a ball
headline: Rain washout: Bangladesh reach Asian Games semi-finals without playing a ball
summary: Higher rankings propel Bangladesh and Sri Lanka to the last four after quarter-final matches are abandoned due to persistent rain in Nagoya.
details: Bangladesh and Sri Lanka have advanced to the men's cricket semi-finals of the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games after their quarter-final matches were abandoned without a single ball being bowled.
Bangladesh was scheduled to play Malaysia, while Sri Lanka was set to face Nepal. Due to persistent rain at the Korogi Sports Park, the higher-ranked teams progressed automatically.
Bangladesh will now face Pakistan in the semi-finals on Thursday. Sri Lanka is set to take on the defending champions, India.
The team will be without batter Najmul Hossain Shanto, who has been ruled out of the tournament due to a fever and infection.
Sports director Jarrad Shearer expressed disappointment over the weather, noting that organizers spent a year converting a baseball diamond into a cricket venue only to see minimal action.
Organizers are now working to dry the grounds using soppers, squeegees, and sponges, hoping for sunny weather to ensure the semi-finals can proceed.
caption:
No balls bowled, but they're through! 🇧🇩

Bangladesh advances to the Asian Games semi-finals thanks to their ranking.

Bangladesh and Sri Lanka have advanced to the men's cricket semi-finals of the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games after their quarter-final matches were abandoned without a single ball being bowled.

Bangladesh was scheduled to play Malaysia, while Sri Lanka was set to face Nepal. Due to persistent rain at the Korogi Sports Park, the higher-ranked teams progressed automatically.

Bangladesh will now face Pakistan in the semi-finals on Thursday. Sri Lanka is set to take on the defending champions, India.

The team will be without batter Najmul Hossain Shanto, who has been ruled out of the tournament due to a fever and infection.

Sports director Jarrad Shearer expressed disappointment over the weather, noting that organizers spent a year converting a baseball diamond into a cricket venue only to see minimal action.

Organizers are now working to dry the grounds using soppers, squeegees, and sponges, hoping for sunny weather to ensure the semi-finals can proceed.

headline_marked: Deep depression near Myanmar: [[Signal 3 issued for Chattogram and Cox's Bazar]]
headline: Deep depression near Myanmar: Signal 3 issued for Chattogram and Cox's Bazar
summary: The Meteorological Department has raised local warning signals as a deep depression moves north-northwest toward the Myanmar coast.
details: A deep depression currently located over the North Andaman Sea and the Myanmar coast is moving in a north-northwest direction, according to the Meteorological Department.
In response to the weather system, local warning signal number 3 has been hoisted for the Chattogram and Cox's Bazar sea ports.
The department stated that the depression may cross the coast of Myanmar and the Kyiaikto area within the next 2 to 3 hours.
Previously, remote warning signal number 1 was in place for Chattogram, Cox's Bazar, Mongla, and Payra ports, which has now been lowered.
Fishing boats and trawlers in the North Bay of Bengal have been advised not to venture into the deep sea or the northeast Bay of Bengal until further notice.
caption:

The department stated that the depression may cross the coast of Myanmar and the Kyiaikto area within the next 2 to 3 hours.

Previously, remote warning signal number 1 was in place for Chattogram, Cox's Bazar, Mongla, and Payra ports, which has now been lowered.

Fishing boats and trawlers in the North Bay of Bengal have been advised not to venture into the deep sea or the northeast Bay of Bengal until further notice.
